speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and feeling bloated. Have you noticed if your stools are pale, clay-colored, or if they smell very foul?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I need to ask: Have you noticed if your urine is very dark or tea-colored? Also, has the baby had any episodes of vomiting bile or passing "currant jelly" stools?

REQUEST TEST: Liver function panel, Bilirubin fractions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the results; normal liver function helps rule out biliary atresia. Given the abdominal distension and pain, have you noticed any visible veins on the baby's abdomen or a "sausage-shaped" mass in the belly? Also, has there been any change in stool consistency, such as "currant jelly" stools?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound.
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdomen

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound and lab results are reassuring so far. Given the distension and pain, have you noticed if the baby has passed any air or stool since the symptoms started, or do they seem to pass gas only with difficulty?

Also, has there been any history of jaundice in the first week of life, or do you notice any lumps in the neck or groin area?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray (supine and upright).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception

Given the ultrasound and X-ray showing dilated bowel with an obstructed rectum, this confirms a mechanical blockage. Please ensure the baby is kept NPO and I will prepare for an urgent air-contrast enema, which serves as both a diagnostic tool and a potential treatment to reduce the telescoped bowel.
